name: Cursor
h1: Cursor ARR: $4B+ and a $60B Acquisition by SpaceX.
intro: Anysphere's AI code editor went from a $1M run rate in 2023 to more than $4 billion in annualized revenue by June 2026 — and then agreed to a $60 billion all-stock acquisition by SpaceX. Every publicly reported revenue, funding and valuation number is collected below, each traced back to a source.

facts.label: Product
facts.value: AI-native code editor and coding agent

modelParagraphs: Cursor sells developer seats. A free tier gets people writing code inside the editor, a Pro plan around $20/month unlocks the frontier models, and business plans add seat management, pooled usage and privacy controls. Because the buyer is an individual engineer first, adoption spreads inside a company long before procurement is involved.

On top of seats sits usage: heavy agent runs consume model tokens, and Cursor bills the overage. That is also the margin pressure point — the company pays frontier labs for inference, so gross margin depends on routing work to the cheapest model that still ships correct code.

faqs.a: Cursor surpassed $4 billion in annualized revenue by June 2026, up from $2 billion in February 2026. That implies roughly $333 million of monthly recurring revenue, and press reports around the acquisition pointed to a forecast above $6 billion by the end of 2026.

faqs.q: How Fast Did Cursor Reach $100M ARR?
faqs.a: About twelve months from its first meaningful revenue — at the time a record pace, later beaten by Lovable's eight months.

faqs.q: Did SpaceX Really Buy Cursor for $60 Billion?
faqs.a: Reuters reported in June 2026 that SpaceX agreed to acquire Anysphere, Cursor's parent, in a $60 billion all-stock deal, days after SpaceX's own IPO. The deal began as an option: in April 2026 SpaceX offered to either buy the company later in the year or pay a $10 billion fee, preempting a planned $2 billion fundraise.

faqs.q: What Was Cursor's Valuation Before the Acquisition?
faqs.a: A $2.3 billion Series D led by Accel and Coatue in November 2025 valued Anysphere at $29.3 billion. By April 2026 the company was in talks to raise at roughly $50 billion — the SpaceX deal then cleared that mark at $60 billion.

faqs.q: Why Do Developers Pay for Cursor When the Models Are Available Elsewhere?
faqs.a: Cursor sells the editor and agent workflow around the models, not the models themselves. Pricing is mostly per-seat — a free tier, a Pro plan around $20/month and business plans with seat management — with usage-heavy agent work billed on top and enterprise contracts following bottom-up adoption.
